To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quiet- sun atmosphere is a complex dynamical system that exhibits a mix of global modes, locally excited waves and subsurface wave sources, and that this dynamical activity is strongly modi ed by subsurface wave diff- raction.

the quiet-sun photosphere and chromosphere contain a large number of short-duration wave sources, that the wave sources are distributed over a wide range of spatial scales, and that the wave sources and the resulting waves are strongly inhomogeneously distributed in the photosphere.

the small-scale topology is a mixture of global modes and waves excited at the photospheric surface and at subsurface layers, with the latter being the main contributor to the observed small-scale dynamics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the topology of the solar small-scale dynamical phenomena and their relation to subsurface wave generation and wave propagation in the quiet Sun.
the small-scale topology (spatial and spectral) of dynamical phenomena, in particular of waves and wave sources in the solar atmosphere.
the small-scale topology and the statistical properties of the wave eld in the solar atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed wave patterns are consistent with the presence of subsur- face wave sources which are excited in a random manner and which are subsequently diffracted by the inhomogeneous sub- surface convection.
we have found no convincing evidence for any particular type of wave source or wave propagation in the internetwork, neither in the photosphere nor in the overlying chromosphere.
there are many different wave modes, and that the observed wave patterns are a result of the interaction between them, and between them and the convective inhomoge- neities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the small-scale topology in the internetwork atmosphere is dominated by the presence of wave sources, wave dissipation, and wave diffraction, which all act to produce the small-scale structure observed in the photosphere, the chromosphere, and the corona.
the observed small-scale dynamics of the solar atmosphere are the result of a complex mix of wave sources and wave propagation.

the observed topology of small-scale dynamical phenomena in quiet-sun intern- work is a result of a combination of subsurface wave excitation, subsurface wave diffractions by convection, and of the superposition of global wave modes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed topology is a result of the interplay of the global modes and the locally excited waves, and that the latter are a consequence of the presence of subsurf- ace wave sources.
the topology of Fourier amplitude maps is complex, and that it can only be understood by taking into account the physics of wave sources and of wave diffraction.
the observed wave modes and their spatial distributions are not consistent with the simple picture of a single global mode.
